title: Rework worker backpressure strategy and retry budget for async queues
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Our current async worker stack suffers from retry storms and unbounded concurrency during traffic spikes. We use a mix of Redis Streams for short-lived jobs and Redis pub/sub for routing which causes sharp queue lag and elevated tail latencies when downstream systems (model serving, external APIs) are transiently slow. Observed symptoms include increased error rates, workers saturating at 100% CPU/GPU, and large numbers of duplicate work due to immediate retries.

Goal: Rework queue consumer/backpressure and retry semantics so the platform degrades gracefully under burst load, limits retry amplification, and provides clear signals to clients and operators. We want a safe rollout path that can be toggled per-queue and per-customer tier.
acceptance_criteria: Per-queue token-bucket concurrency limiter implemented with configurable burst and steady rates
Retry budget implemented per job-type with sliding-window accounting and enforced cap on retry attempts
Exponential backoff with full jitter applied to worker retries and documented default parameters
Kafka consumer group adapter implemented for high-throughput queues with idempotency support and at-least-once semantics validated
Client-facing backpressure: 429 + Retry-After returned when queue write-rate exceeds configured ingress budgets
Instrumentation: queue lag, retry ratio, retry budget utilization, and worker concurrency exported to Datadog and dashboard added
Two-phase rollout behind feature flags (canary on non-prod, 10% traffic, full rollout) with auto-rollback on SLO regressions
Benchmarks show reduction in retry storms and tail latency under synthetic spike tests (see updates)
updates: 2026-02-21: Spike investigation notes added to Confluence; linked failing runbooks for incidents in Jan/Feb

2026-02-25: Design review with Reliability and Runtime teams. Decided to adopt Kafka consumer groups for high-throughput paths and keep Redis Streams for low-volume control-plane jobs to minimize migration blast radius
2026-03-02: Prototype of token-bucket limiter checked in (runtime/worker/limiter) and feature-flagged. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289

2026-03-05: Initial load test against prototype: synthetic 5x traffic spike. Observed 58% reduction in failed retries and 32% reduction in P99 processing latency for the tested queue (details in performance doc)
2026-03-08: UX for client backpressure (429 + Retry-After) agreed with API team. Draft API contract: /enqueue responses include backoff_hint header

2026-03-10: Started Kafka adapter integration branch. Added idempotency token handling and retention policy for dedupe cache. Open PR planned for 2026-03-14: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1304
notes: Trade-offs: Kafka gives durable, partitioned ordering and consumer rebalancing at scale but increases operational complexity. We will run Kafka only for queues with >1000 msgs/min; keep Redis for remaining queues.
Retry budget model: budget replenishes at a configurable rate per job-type. Budget exhaustion will mark job as 'deferred' and either move to slow-path processing or poison queue depending on policy.

Backpressure signaling: prefer explicit 429 over silent drop. Downstream clients (Console/SDK) will implement exponential client-side retry with server-provided hint. This avoids large retry storms from naive clients.

Idempotency: add idempotency token header to job payloads. Workers must dedupe via a short-lived Redis cache for cross-consumer dedupe during at-least-once processing. Consider moving to RocksDB store if Redis cost/latency becomes an issue.

Open question: exact default retry parameters (initial_backoff, max_backoff, max_attempts). Proposal: initial=500ms, max=30s, max_attempts=5 with full jitter. Need sign-off from Product on customer-visible retry behavior.
Rollout plan: feature-flag per-queue, metric gates (retry_ratio < 5% and queue_lag stable) for automated progression. Manual rollback via flag if error budget consumed.
Security: no new high-sensitivity data stored in retry budgets. Review scheduled if dedupe cache retention extends beyond 24h.
